top_stories.title: Building self-improving tax agents with Codex
top_stories.summary: OpenAI details how Codex is being used to build self-improving AI agents capable of handling complex tax workflows, representing a significant step in applying agentic AI to professional services. The post outlines how these agents iteratively refine their own performance, pointing toward a new model of AI-assisted knowledge work. This is a primary source announcement from OpenAI's official blog.

top_stories.title: Millions of AI agents imperiled by critical vulnerability in open source package
top_stories.summary: Ars Technica reports that a critical security vulnerability in a widely used open source package puts millions of AI agents at risk of compromise. The flaw could allow attackers to manipulate or intercept agent behaviour at scale, raising serious concerns about the security foundations of the rapidly growing agentic AI ecosystem.

top_stories.title: Rethinking organizational design in the age of agentic AI [Metered]
top_stories.summary: MIT Technology Review examines how the rise of agentic AI is forcing companies to reconsider their organisational structures, workflows, and management hierarchies. The piece argues that agentic systems are not just productivity tools but structural forces that reshape how decisions are made and how teams are composed.

top_stories.title: Robinhood will let your AI agent trade stocks and make (or lose) lots of money
top_stories.summary: Robinhood is launching a feature that allows AI agents to autonomously execute stock trades on behalf of users, marking a significant expansion of agentic AI into consumer finance. The Verge reports that the move raises both excitement about automated investing and serious questions about accountability when AI-driven trades go wrong.

top_stories.title: Fake academic journals are publishing AI-generated papers under real professors' names
top_stories.summary: A report reveals that fraudulent academic journals are using AI to generate research papers and publishing them under the names of real academics without their knowledge or consent. The trend represents a serious threat to research integrity, combining concerns about AI-generated content with predatory publishing practices.

further_links.title: Why the Vatican Invited Anthropic to the Pope's AI Encyclical Presentation [Metered]
further_links.summary: Wired reports on Anthropic's involvement in the Vatican's unveiling of Pope Leo XIV's encyclical on AI, shedding light on the unusual relationship between the Catholic Church and Silicon Valley AI labs.

further_links.title: What Pope Leo XIV's First Encyclical Says About the Power of AI [Metered]
further_links.summary: Wired analyses the content of the Pope's encyclical, which addresses the ethical and societal implications of artificial intelligence and calls for human dignity to be placed at the centre of technological development.

further_links.title: The AI fight brewing inside The New York Times
further_links.summary: The Verge reports on tensions at The New York Times between management and the Tech Guild union over the use of AI tools to monitor journalist performance, highlighting broader debates about AI, labour, and editorial autonomy.

further_links.title: Former Google and Apple Researchers Launch a Startup to Build AI's Missing Feedback Loop [Metered]
further_links.summary: Wired profiles a new startup founded by ex-Google and Apple researchers aiming to build AI systems that improve continuously through user interaction, addressing a key limitation of current static models.

further_links.title: YouTube is putting AI labels where you'll actually see them
further_links.summary: YouTube is updating its AI content disclosure system to make labels more prominent and visible to viewers, particularly on Shorts, as part of broader efforts to improve transparency around synthetic media.

further_links.title: The AI bubble isn't like the internet bubble
further_links.summary: Cory Doctorow at Pluralistic argues that the current AI investment bubble has structural differences from the dot-com era, with implications for how and when it might deflate and who bears the costs.

further_links.title: The Download: puncturing the AI jobs panic [Metered]
further_links.summary: MIT Technology Review examines the latest data on AI's impact on employment, finding that the widespread fear of immediate mass job displacement may be overstated by current evidence.

further_links.title: AI tried to bury this politician — now people have actually heard of him
further_links.summary: The Verge reports on a New York politician whose profile was suppressed in AI-generated search results, but whose story went viral after the suppression was publicised, raising questions about AI's influence on political visibility.

further_links.title: CIOs are enlisting business users to vibe code their own apps
further_links.summary: A report describes how IT leaders are encouraging non-technical staff to use AI coding tools to build their own internal applications, accelerating software delivery while raising questions about governance and quality.

further_links.title: Bay Area mom out thousands after scammers use AI to mimic daughter's voice
further_links.summary: ABC7 News reports on a case where scammers used AI voice cloning to impersonate a woman's daughter in a fake kidnapping scheme, illustrating the growing threat of AI-enabled fraud targeting consumers.

ethan_mollick.title: Choosing to Stay Human
ethan_mollick.summary: Ethan Mollick explores the tension between embracing AI capabilities and deliberately choosing to preserve human effort, skill, and experience in an age where AI can increasingly do tasks for us. He argues that the question of when to use AI and when to opt out is becoming one of the defining personal and social choices of our time, with implications for identity, learning, and what we value in human endeavour.
